tspan.tspan: Ever wondered what your muscles look like?
Take a peek beneath the skin with ultrasound imaging.
Ultrasound is widely used in sports science, biomechanics, and
rehabilitation. It can be used to study muscle architecture and

text.tspan: tendon behaviour or to assess injuries and monitor recovery.

tspan.tspan: An ultrasound transducer is placed on the skin over a muscle. It
captures live images of the tissues beneath the skin. You can watch

text.tspan: your own muscles change shape as you move, flex, and relax.

tspan.tspan: Ultrasound imaging uses a handheld device called a transducer to
send sound waves into the body and detect echoes returning from
tissues. Different tissues reflect sound differently, allowing muscles,

text.tspan: tendons, fat, and bone to be distinguished in the image.
